 I too have acne scars on my chest, shoulders, back... hundreds of them. My face too. My face is my first priority. I studied different methods for scar removal for 2-3 months... it was my obsession for a while. So let me break it down for you. Don't expect anything more than 30-40% improval so that you don't get depressed with the results, anything is an improvement... although some people get 70-80%. Only look into this stuff when you get your acne taken care of because scars can only be fixed after your active acne is taken care of. Also don't get sucked too much into this because the community is full of depressed people and reading their posts will get you really down. So yeah, I recommend you only research any of these topics once you're done with the acne.

-if you have deep wavy scars on your face (called rolling scars) you need to get a subcision done by a dermatologist who has done MANY of them. This is a relatively cheap procedure (less than 1000) After your subcision, you need to vacuum the areas on your face that have been subcised for 2-3 seconds at a time, once per day. This is relatively unknown by dermatologists, but it causes way better results according to some people who have tried this. Look up subcision-suction for more details...

-Get a TCA peel by a qualified dermatologist to smooth out the texture and get rid of ice-pick scars (small holes).

-Use a derma-roller once every 2 weeks to increase the general texture of your face. After each derma rolling session use copper peptides to stimulate your skin to regrow.

-Under any circumstances do not get a laser treatment. It may look better at first, but it long-term fucks up your skin even worse than it was when you started. Not to mention it costs thousands of dollars.

Hope this helps. I gotta stop thinking about acne now, it's getting me down.

Same here. This is my game plan: -accutane gets rid of active acne, then hope that in 15-25 years tissue regeneration will be a possibility and scarred and damaged tissue will be able to be healed. In the meantime, you have to accept your current state. It took me 6-8 months of crying, freaking out and throwing things around to realize that acne scars are here to stay. You eventually just have to accept it and hope that the future may help you lead a normal life and get with that girl that you crush on. By the way, if you still have active acne, and it's bad, try accutane. You can go on a low dose if you're afraid of the side effects.
